statement: When a scanner stops evaluating a regex taken from untrusted input, time the regex that finds that input as well. Cejel compiled a repository's `pnpm run /<regex>/` selector and tested it against the repository's own script names, so `/^(a+)+$/` stalled the scan. The literal that captured the selector, `\/((?:\\.|[^/])+)\/`, could read each backslash two ways: 40 unterminated backslashes took 1.1 s, rising about 1.6 times per character. The repository's literal-ReDoS guard missed it because none of its adversarial input families contains a backslash run. Rule: prove the whole scan path is bounded with a child-process timing guard, since a stalled V8 regex cannot be interrupted inside its own thread. Treat a family-based ReDoS guard as covering only the families it runs.
